scenes.headline: How a 320B model gets quantized for a Mac
scenes.sub: OrcaSAQ's five MLX builds of GLM-5.3-Flash, and what fits where.
scenes.say: Hi, I'm Spruce! Here's how a three-hundred-twenty-billion-parameter model gets quantized for Apple Silicon, and which Macs it actually fits.

scenes.text: OrcaSAQ sets each tensor's bits from its role in the architecture, with no calibration data, and only re-quantizes what FP8 already quantized.
scenes.mark: from its role in the architecture
scenes.say: The idea: no calibration data. Each tensor's bit budget follows from its role in the architecture, and only tensors FP8 already quantized can move.

scenes.title: One rule for eligibility, three for bits

steps.say: OrcaSAQ starts from the official FP8 release, and asks every tensor one question: did it ship with a scale? That makes it eligible.
If not, it stays BF16 in every build: the thirty-four linear-attention layers, the indexer, the norms, the vision tower.
Eligible expert and sparse-attention projections get the tier's base bit width. The tensor's role decides, not a calibration run.
Down projections, the most sensitive to rounding, get one bit more. The shared expert, which fires on every token, gets two more.

scenes.title: Five builds, file size in GB
scenes.say: That gives five builds, from a near-lossless six-bit at two hundred ninety-six gigabytes down to the two-bit lite at a hundred and two.

scenes.quote: everything down to 3-bit degrades gently, 2-bit costs a lot, and 2bit-lite costs a lot more. Pick it for fit, not for quality.
scenes.mark: Pick it for fit, not for quality.
scenes.say: Perplexity, KL divergence and cosine similarity all agree where the cliff is. The README says it plainly: below three bits, pick it for fit, not for quality.

scenes.label: Mac memory tiers that can load any build: 128GB, with a manual workaround
scenes.note: 2bit-lite was verified on an H200, not a Mac
scenes.say: And fit is narrow. Of nine Mac memory tiers, only the top one fits any build, with its wired-memory limit raised by hand.

scenes.text: Below three bits, a build is a size tier, not a value tier: sold on what it fits, not what it preserves.

recap: A tensor's role sets its bits
2bit-lite fits one Mac tier, by hand
scenes.say: To recap: quantize only what FP8 did, set bits by role, and choose the smallest build for fit, not quality.
